newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel says PLO must have only pistols in Hebron.
newsitem.headline: Israel says PLO must have only pistols in Hebron.

text.p: Israeli Defence Minister Yitzhak Mordechai confirmed in an interview published on Friday that Israel wanted changes to the accord on Hebron between the Palestinians and the previous government.
Israeli leaders had denied Palestinian charges they wanted to change terms of the accord under which Israel was to reduce its troops in the West Bank town of Hebron.
Mordechai's statement was the first official Israeli confirmation it wanted Palestinian police due to be stationed in Hebron not to have rifles, changing the original agreement.
Israel's Jerusalem Post daily asked him if Israel was demanding at the negotiations which began on Sunday that Palestine Liberation Organisation (PLO) police in Hebron carry only pistols.
"Yes," he replied, "We understandably want to reduce the scale and types of weapons to reduce the dangers that could likely happen."

Israel's government ousted by right-wing Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu in May elections signed a self-rule deal in September 1995 that said up to 400 Palestinian policemen armed with 200 pistols and 100 rifles would deploy in certain areas of Hebron.

Mordechai also told the Post that Israel was insisting Palestinian police who fired on Israeli soldiers in clashes last month triggered by Israeli policies in Jerusalem be prosecuted. Fifteen Israelis and 60 Palestinians were killed in the fighting.
Palestinians have said in reply to the Israeli demand for prosecution that the Jewish state should try its troops who fired on Palestinians.

Palestinian police, under the Hebron deal, are to deploy in areas that include ridges that overlook the centre of town where some 400 Jewish settlers live amidst 100,000 Arabs. Israeli troops are to remain to guard the settlers.
Asked if Israel now wanted to control the ridges as Israeli news reports have said, Mordechai said he did not want to enter into details of the current negotiations.
Mordechai said the unprecedented gunbattles last month hardened Israel's resolve to increase security provisions in arrangements stemming from the framework 1993 PLO-Israel peace deal.

"These crises are difficult and cause us to strengthen our guidelines...without the IDF (Israeli army) and security services in every place possible, we are likely to get into very dangerous situations," Mordechai said. He did not elaborate.
Israel's previous government gave most of the Gaza Strip and parts of the West Bank over to Palestinian rule.
A redeployment in Hebron, the only Palestinian town with Israeli settlers in its midst, was to have occurred in March but was delayed after Islamic suicide bombers killed 59 people in Israel.
